In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to produce a mammalian enzyme in a yeast expression system.
the development of an efficient expression and purification system for mammalian AChEs, in particular for the production of the human enzyme.
the functional expression of AChE, a mammalian enzyme, in P. pastoris.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yeast expressed ACH is the most similar to the native AChET.
the P. pastoris expressed enzyme has a higher stability, is less sensitive to inhibition by organophosphorous compounds and is more resistant against heat denaturation.
the functional expression of the rat AChE in E. coli and P. pastoris was achieved, but the E. coli system is not suitable for a large scale production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression in P. pastoris is superior to the expression in E. coli.
the refolding of the bacterial expressed AChE was improved by removing the cysteine and by purification prior to the refolding.
the refolded E. coli AChE is suitable for biochemical studies, while the functional expression of AChE from P. pastoris is a promising approach for large-scale production of AChE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of a functional mammalian enzyme in P. pastoris is a promising alternative to E. coli for the production of mammalian proteins.
the P. pastoris system is a good alternative for the functional expression of the mammalian acetyl cholinesterase.
the expression and purification of recombinant AChE in E. coli is not suitable for large-scale production of active AChEs.
